blogs.title: Dog Bite, White Count Down: Recognizing Capnocytophaga Before the Culture Turns Positive
blogs.description: This post would use the case to review invasive Capnocytophaga canimorsus infection in adults, including why severe disease can occur even in immunocompetent hosts. It would highlight bedside clues such as recent dog exposure, profound leukopenia, DIC, hypoglycaemia, acral ischaemia, and rapidly progressive sepsis, then discuss empiric antibiotic choices and the growing role of molecular diagnostics for this slow-growing organism.

blogs.title: DIC or Something Else? Spotting Sepsis-Triggered TMA Hiding in Plain Sight
blogs.description: This post would focus on the diagnostic pivot from septic coagulopathy to superimposed thrombotic microangiopathy. It would explore how improving infection markers can falsely reassure clinicians while persistent thrombocytopenia, new haemolysis, schistocytosis, and dialysis-dependent AKI signal that DIC is no longer the whole story.

blogs.title: The DAT Trap: Coombs Positivity, Schistocytes, and Mislabeling MAHA as Autoimmune Hemolysis
blogs.description: This post would examine the haemolysis workup in a critically ill patient with a positive direct antiglobulin test. It would review how recent penicillin exposure, transfusions, and critical illness can muddy DAT interpretation, why steroids may be a reflex but not always the right move, and how the blood smear remains pivotal for distinguishing autoimmune haemolysis from microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia.

blogs.title: Normal Complement, Abnormal Endothelium: Diagnosing Complement-Mediated HUS in Adults
blogs.description: This post would offer a practical adult TMA framework centered on excluding TTP and STEC-HUS while recognizing complement-mediated HUS as a diagnosis of exclusion. It would cover PLASMIC scoring, ADAMTS13 interpretation, stool PCR, the limited rule-out value of normal C3 and C4, and how treatment timing can complicate downstream complement and genetic testing.

blogs.title: Biopsy After the Bleeding Stops: When Dialysis-Dependent Septic AKI Needs Kidney Histology
blogs.description: This post would discuss the role of kidney biopsy in persistent severe AKI after sepsis and DIC, especially once thrombocytopenia begins to recover enough for a safer procedure. It would explain how biopsy findings such as fibrin thrombi, ischaemic glomeruli, and concurrent acute tubular necrosis can change management by confirming TMA rather than presumed prolonged septic kidney injury alone.

blogs.title: Blocking Complement After Bacteraemia: Eculizumab Timing, Plasma Exchange, and the Infection Tradeoff
blogs.description: This post would tackle the management tension at the heart of the case: treating complement-mediated HUS with eculizumab when terminal complement blockade may impair host defense against encapsulated bacteria. It would compare the temporary stabilizing role of plasma exchange with the disease-modifying effect of eculizumab, and review timing after culture clearance, meningococcal vaccination, antibiotic prophylaxis, and how to think about treatment duration when genetic testing is negative.
